Twenty distinct pinned Maven package paths passed valid MP4 controls; this reaches the working count but does not establish an exhaustive most-used top 20. The latest paths are Red5 red5-io, com.googlecode.mp4parser:isoparser, org.tallison:isoparser, and com.liferay:org.mp4parser. Red5 reads a valid three-second 16x16 H.264/AAC MP4 and reports parsed keyframe count and codecs; its published POM requests an unavailable mina-core bundle, so the adapter excludes transitive dependencies and pins the needed JARs explicitly. The three additional isoparser distributions and existing org.mp4parser:isoparser/muxer share the MP4Parser underlying family. Tika uses metadata-extractor; seven paths rely on FFmpeg/FFprobe; two use libmediainfo; two use the JAAD family; Red5 uses JCodec. These twenty package paths are therefore not twenty independent parser implementations. Four valid controls cover the original 2x2 H.264/AAC MP4, a padded variant with a valid free box for the amilesend minimum-size API, a metadata-free two-stream variant for JAAD 0.8.7, and a three-second variant for Red5. All control bytes and SHA-256 checks are pinned. Nine bounded Maven Solr queries used 100-result limits. Successful windows saved 128 hits, 122 unique: mp4 saved 100 of 350, mp4 parser six, isoparser four, and Java MP4 18. ISO base media and MP4 demuxer returned zero; JAAD MP4, JavaSound AAC MP4, and red5 mp4 timed out. Earlier successful windows are preserved after refresh timeouts. Most Java MP4 hits use mp for unrelated software; 18 remain unreviewed search hits. Three targeted leads remain unresolved: the MP4Parser streaming module, a Gitee isoparser distribution, and Velvet Video. The MP4Parser aggregate POM, ytk-mp4j, CodecMedia 1.2.2, jaudiotagger 3.0.1, MonteMedia MP4 write-only support, and jcodec-javase 0.2.5 were rejected after documentation checks or failed control runs. The controls establish format-aware parsing for their specific MP4 variants only. Java SE 25 official API documentation yielded no bundled MP4 parser; a JDK-only run found no ImageIO or Java Sound reader for the original control, though third-party providers may add support. No vulnerability, malformed-input or resource-use experiments were run.
